title: Claude Managed Agents and Evolution of Agentic Surfaces — Gagan Bhat & Isabella Kai He, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic engineers describe how agent harnesses evolved from raw messages API to managed agents, arguing harnesses encode stale assumptions about model limits and must be decoupled into swappable primitives. They detail a brain/hands split (agent loop separate from sandbox), durable session logs, credential vaults, and a grader-based 'outcomes' loop.

takeaways.technique: Decouple agent loop from sandbox (brain vs hands)
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the model reasoning loop in a separate process from the tool-execution container so reasoning starts immediately and container setup runs in parallel; if the sandbox dies the brain spins a new one and retries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Separating the brain or the agent loop from the hands or the tool execution environment of the agent.
takeaways.numbers: 60% faster time-to-first-token at P50; >90% improvement at P95

takeaways.technique: Durable session log as recoverable context
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist every event (user msg, model response, tool calls, results) to a durable session resource; when context is compacted or discarded, the harness re-reads slices from the log instead of losing them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the harness can actually just read in slices of that context from the session log into its current window

takeaways.technique: Outcomes: separate grader agent with rubric loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Define success criteria and failure cases as a rubric; a separate grader agent runs alongside the worker, checks the rubric, and the worker keeps iterating until criteria are met.
takeaways.evidence_quote: outcomes essentially starts a separate greater agent that runs alongside your agent loop and looks at whether that agent was actually able to accomplish the task

takeaways.technique: Credential vaults decrypted only at tool runtime
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep secrets in a vault decrypted only at tool-execution time so the model never sees tokens; sandbox networking restricted to allowlisted hosts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep credentials away from your agent and the model never sees your security tokens

takeaways.technique: Dreaming: batch memory consolidation from session logs
takeaways.what_they_do: Periodically batch-process session transcripts plus current memory state to extract insights and rewrite memory, so the next day's sessions start smarter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: feed the transcripts and the memory state as a periodic batch process with what we call dreaming

takeaways.technique: Prune stale harness assumptions on model swaps
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat harness fixes (context resets, compaction) as assumptions about model limits that go stale; remove them when a new model no longer needs them, since dead weight adds latency and breaks caching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the model moves and the harness doesn't, it degrades the agent
